## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Rohaṇamigajātaka* (Ja 501), translated in English as *The Golden Deer*, is a narrative text preserved in the *Jātaka* collection of the Khuddaka Nikāya. In its introductory frame narrative set at the Bamboo Grove (Veḷuvana), the Buddha addresses the assembly of monks discussing the Venerable Ānanda's self-sacrificing devotion in renouncing his life for the Teacher. The Buddha remarks that this was not the first occasion Ānanda had placed his life in peril for him, prompting the narration of the story of the past. The story concerns a virtuous deer and concludes with an exhortation delivered to an earthly monarch, counseling righteous governance toward courtiers and subjects so as to attain heaven [Tambiah 1976].
